newsitem.title: ITALY: Italian decree to boost jobs due next week - union.
newsitem.headline: Italian decree to boost jobs due next week - union.

text.p: An Italian government decree law aimed at speeding up investment to create new jobs will be passed next week, said Sergio D'Antoni, leader of the CISL trades union confederation.
D'Antoni told a news conference after a meeting with government ministers that a cabinet meeting on Friday was examining the measures that "will be passed next week."
Also, union officials said the government was working on an amendment to a package put together by Labour Minister Tiziano Treu that will go before the Senate upper house on Tuesday.

The package of measures, which includes provisions aimed at cutting the working week, introducing more flexible work contracts and boosting apprenticeship schemes, was agreed upon by majority party leaders and the hard-left on Thursday.
The centre-left government struck a deal on Thursday with parliamentary ally Communist Refoundation over disputed employment issues, easing tensions within the coalition.

Deputy Prime Minister Walter Veltroni told reporters the accord, reached after a four hour meeting between the heads of coalition parties and Refoundation leader Fausto Bertinotti had strengthened the 10-month old government.
Bertinotti said the deal meant that 100,000 new jobs would be created for young people in the underdeveloped south.
The amendment to the Treu package will increase by 300 billion lire ($176.6 million) the resources already earmarked for a so-called employment fund, which will total some 1.9 trillion lire.
The decree, on the other hand, will contain measures simplifying procedures fo free up public expenditure on jobs.

Union leaders said after their meeting with government on Friday that steps forward on the jobs front had been made but confirmed their aim to hold a day of nationwide rallies in favour of employment on March 22.
"We're finally seeing some concrete commitment, but we're still a long way off satisfactory results. So, we are still going to hold the March 22 rally," D'Antoni said.
